digest.component_or_area: autolander bot lifecycle: heartbeat, liveness check, emergency-stop, drain, and crash-safe recovery
propositions: The bot must write a heartbeat timestamp file once per 15-second poll cycle; freshness is exposed as heartbeat_age_s via the status endpoint and must stay below 15 seconds during normal operation.

A Docker HEALTHCHECK with stat-based local heartbeat age verification must mark the container unhealthy if heartbeat age exceeds 90 seconds (without probing Gerrit), triggering autoheal restart only when truly hung.
An emergency-stop sentinel file on the state volume must gate the bot into paused phase when present, preventing new Autosubmit selection; removal resumes normal operation without redeploy.

On SIGTERM, the bot must write recovery.json (change_id, chain_member_ids, tested_shas, phase, re_drive_count, acknowledged flag) as the first action before drain, ensuring crash-safe recovery independent of subsequent interruptions.

During the drain window, the bot must keep heartbeating each tick so the HEALTHCHECK remains healthy and autoheal is not provoked mid-drain; recovery.json written first ensures idempotency even if autoheal restarts mid-drain.

On restart, the bot must reconcile recovery.json against live Gerrit and S3 state before selecting new work, implementing phase-specific rules (rebasing/awaiting_verified: re-select; submitting: check merged status or re-drive; idle/paused: proceed normally) to prevent double-submit and stranded stacks.
